documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Back on full duty since the fall, climbing scaffolds again, though he says he's done with ladders when someone younger can go up. Right knee occasionally stiff after a long day, otherwise no limitation. Discharged from ortho and PT.
No chest symptoms, no palpitations. No cough or shortness of breath on amiodarone. RA quiet.
PHQ-2 0. Sleeps well.
Exam: BMI about 28. HEENT normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Right knee: healed midline scar, full extension, flexion to about 125, strength 5/5. Hands without synovitis. Skin clear.
A/P
- Quad tendon rupture, repaired and recovered. Off the active list; surgery stays in history.
- HTN, RA, hx VT on amiodarone: all stable, labs today incl. TSH.
- Vaccines up to date for the season. Colonoscopy due next year, will refer at next physical.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check. No new problems. Allergies acting up with the pollen this spring, same as every year. Meds unchanged, adherent, uses a weekly pill box with a separate Saturday slot for the methotrexate.
Exam: well. Heart regular, slow-normal rate. Lungs clear, no crackles. No edema.
A/P: All stable. LFTs and CBC today. Next TSH with the physical. Rheum in July. RTC fall for flu and COVID.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 07/18/2023

Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, well controlled. Brief hand stiffness in the morning only. No rash, fevers or other features of lupus since 2021. Recovered well from the quadriceps tendon repair last year.
Medications: methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, amiodarone 200 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: no synovitis; no deformity; skin clear.
Recent labs through PCP reviewed, normal.
Plan: no change. Labs every 3 months. Return in one year, sooner for flares.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No-show for 3:00 follow-up. Left voicemail to reschedule. Pt texted back later: stuck on a job site with an inspection, apologized, will book with his flu shot.

documents.title: Vaccines and lab draw
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza IM left deltoid and 2023-24 Moderna IM right deltoid. Rheum standing labs drawn. Rebooked the missed September follow-up into the physical in February since nothing is changing; PCP agreed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical. Feeling well, no new symptoms. Joints controlled. Knee fine. No breathing complaints on amiodarone, no palpitations. Sees cardiology in early April.
PHQ-2 1, tired from the winter, nothing more.
Exam: BMI ~28. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Extremities without edema, calves symmetric. Skin: no lesions of concern.
A/P
- HTN at goal on lisinopril/amlodipine.
- Seropositive RA on MTX/prednisone/folate, rheum yearly.
- Hx VT on amiodarone, TSH and LFTs today.
- Colonoscopy due (last 2014, normal): GI referral placed.
- PSA after discussion, lipids, CMP, CBC today.
- Vaccines: PCV20 and Shingrix done; flu/COVID current.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group
Procedure date: 02/27/2024
Indication: screening, prior normal colonoscopy 2014, no family history of colorectal cancer.
Prep: good (BBPS 8). Cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Withdrawal time 9 minutes.
Findings: normal colonic mucosa throughout. No polyps.
Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: next screening in 10 years.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: New fill: warfarin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fill history update shows warfarin 5 mg tablets dispensed 4/5, prescribed by his cardiologist. Nothing from cardiology in the chart about why. Message to pt asking him to call, and records request to cardiology.

reports.text: Left lower extremity venous duplex with compression and color Doppler. The deep veins of the left calf are noncompressible and distended with echogenic intraluminal thrombus and absent flow, consistent with acute thrombus. The common femoral, femoral and popliteal veins are compressible with normal phasic flow. Superficial veins without thrombus.
reports.conclusion: Acute deep vein thrombosis of the left calf veins.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED
Visit: 04/15/2024

CC: left calf swelling.
HPI: 60 year old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed by his cardiologist 10 days ago and started on warfarin, history of procainamide-induced lupus, seropositive RA, and prior quadriceps tendon rupture. Two days of swelling and mild aching in the left calf. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or recent injury. No herbal supplements.
PMH: hypertension, seropositive RA, paroxysmal AF, history of VT, seasonal allergies, drug-induced lupus, H. pylori, quadriceps tendon rupture.
PSH: repair of right quadriceps tendon.
Meds: warfarin as directed by cardiology, amiodarone 200 mg daily, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: occasional alcohol, nonsmoker.

Vitals within normal limits.
Exam: left lower leg warm and red, tender along the back of the calf, mild pitting edema. Right leg normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear.
Labs: INR 3.1. CBC and BMP unremarkable.
Duplex: acute DVT, left calf.

Assessment: acute deep vein thrombosis of the left lower extremity, on warfarin.
Plan: continue current medications including warfarin; anticoagulation clinic to recheck INR this week; leg elevation; routine follow-up with PCP and cardiology. Return for chest pain or shortness of breath.

conditions.label: Acute deep vein thrombosis of left lower extremity

medications.sig: Take as directed by anticoagulation clinic, usually 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth daily, adjusted per INR

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED Monday for left calf DVT. Filling in what we didn't have: at his cardiology visit on 4/5 an ECG showed atrial fibrillation; he felt nothing. Cardiologist started warfarin that day, managed by their anticoagulation clinic. We never got a note.
Calf a bit less swollen today, still sore climbing stairs. No chest pain, no breathlessness, no hemoptysis. Taking warfarin as told; clinic rechecked INR yesterday and adjusted, he isn't sure of the number.
Exam: left calf mildly swollen and tender posteriorly, warmth less than described in the ED. Right leg normal. Heart regular today. Lungs clear. SpO2 normal.
A/P
1. Paroxysmal AF, new, on warfarin per cardiology; continues amiodarone. Added to list.
2. Acute left calf DVT, already anticoagulated. Continue warfarin, INR through cardiology's clinic. Walking encouraged, elevate when sitting. ED and duplex reviewed.
3. Med list updated. Requested cardiology note again.
Recheck in about 4 months, sooner if the leg worsens or any chest or breathing symptoms.

documents.title: Anticoagulation clinic update
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Anticoagulation clinic, outside cardiology group.
Indication: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; left calf DVT 04/2024. Goal INR 2-3.
After early high readings, dose adjusted; INR now stable in range on the current weekly warfarin schedule. Most recent INR 06/07. Next check in 4 weeks.

conditions.note: symptoms resolved after 4 months of anticoagulation

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Left calf back to normal for about a month, no swelling at end of day. INRs in range per the anticoagulation clinic. No bleeding, no bruising beyond the usual from work. No palpitations.
Exam: calves symmetric, nontender, no edema. Heart regular. Lungs clear.
A/P
1. Left calf DVT, resolved clinically; moved to history. Warfarin continues for AF per cardiology.
2. PAF on amiodarone and warfarin. TSH, LFTs, CBC today.
3. HTN, RA unchanged.
Flu/COVID in October. Physical February.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: On warfarin: fine-gauge needle, firm pressure 2 minutes at each site. High-dose flu L deltoid (immunosuppressed, PCP order), Pfizer 2024-25 R deltoid. No bleeding or reaction.

documents.title: Cardiology letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group
Re: Mark Barrett, follow-up 11/2024

History of ventricular tachycardia on amiodarone 200 mg daily since 10/2020 after procainamide-induced lupus. At his 04/05/2024 visit a resting ECG showed atrial fibrillation; asymptomatic. Started warfarin 5 mg daily, adjusted per INR, through our anticoagulation clinic. He had a left calf DVT on 04/15/2024 on warfarin with an INR of 3.1; anticoagulation continued.
Today without palpitations or other symptoms. Plan: continue amiodarone and warfarin. TSH and liver tests every six months through PCP. Return in one year.
Allergies: NKDA.
Medications: amiodarone 200 mg daily, warfarin per clinic, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg, prednisone 5 mg.
